I had this kind of ego thing where I
loved being the most valuable player, right? I loved being able to come in and
save the day, and put the team on my back, and everyone's like, "Rocky,
Rocky, you know, whatever, right?" But, what a terrible thing to want if you
want to have a business. It's one thing to be able to sell, it's another thing
to be able to teach to sell. It's one thing to be able to train, another thing
to be able to teach to train. One thing to be able to run ads, another thing to
be able to teach people to run ads. And so, before this, it was like, "Oh, they
went two for six today. I can go in and close five out of six." Okay, cool.
Well, that means that you suck as a teacher, not that you're great as a
sales guy. And so, I had to shift my identity to being, "I want to be the
best sales teacher, marketing teacher, operations teacher," right? And by doing
that, it shifted how I saw what winning looked like.
